Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates enlargement of the central pulmonary arteries, specifically a prominent right descending pulmonary artery (pruned appearance), which is a classic radiographic sign of pulmonary hypertension associated with chronic thromboembolic disease. The cardiac silhouette appears relatively normal in size, suggesting the hypertension is present but perhaps not yet causing massive right heart failure, fitting the description of mild to moderate pulmonary hypertension rather than severe decompensation.
